                continue;
            }
            if (word_index < MAX_WORD_LENGTH) {
                word[word_index++] = (char)c;
            } else {
                overflow = true;
            }
        }
    }
}

My earlier framing was wrong, and the byte counts prove it. Let me give you the arithmetic before the code.

`"echo hello from user mode"` is **25 characters**. With a 20-byte *line* buffer it truncates to `"echo hello from use"`, and no amount of whitespace normalization can recover the missing `r mode`. So `msh-echo` is unpassable under the constraint as I stated it.

But the tests and the constraint are compatible — the 20 bytes is a **word** limit, not a line limit. The fix is to stop buffering the whole line:

| test | longest token |
|---|---|
| `msh-echo` | `hello` (5) |
| `msh-editing` | `argument` (8) |
| `hw1-echo` | `goodbye` (7) |
| `msh-overlong` | `aaa…` (136) → **must** overflow |

Every command word and every echo argument fits in 20 bytes. Only the overlong line exceeds it — which is exactly what that test checks. So the reference implementation streams words as they complete, and the buffer holds one token at a time. That's why the 20-byte spec and the 25-byte echo input don't actually conflict.

This also explains the expected output shape: it's not live echo (no `echx\bo` artifact appears), and blank/leading-space lines emit no newline — so words must be dispatched individually, not as a stored line.

## Plan — rewrite the buffering as word-at-a-time

The `.bss` footprint stays at 21 bytes, so there's no tick-budget regression. Replace `buffer`/`buffer_index`/`overflow` with:

```c
#define MAX_WORD_LENGTH 20

static char word[MAX_WORD_LENGTH + 1];
static size_t word_index = 0;
static bool overflow = false;
static bool command_resolved = false;
static bool echo_mode = false;
static bool echo_started = false;
static bool line_output = false;

static void write_bytes(const char *str, size_t length) {
    ioctl(MINEMU_FD_UART_OUT, MINEMU_IOCTL_UART_WRITE, str, length);
}

static void write_string(const char *str) {
    size_t length = 0;
    while (str[length] != '\0') {
        ++length;
    }
    write_bytes(str, length);
}

static void line_reset(void) {
    word_index = 0;
    overflow = false;
    command_resolved = false;
    echo_mode = false;
    echo_started = false;
    line_output = false;
}

static void finish_word(bool line_end) {
    word[word_index] = '\0';
    size_t length = word_index;
    word_index = 0;

    if (overflow) {                       /* overlong line: discard entirely */
        if (line_end) {
            line_reset();
        }
        return;
    }

    if (!command_resolved) {
        if (length != 0) {                /* leading spaces resolve nothing */
            command_resolved = true;
            if (length == 4 && word[0] == 'e' && word[1] == 'c' &&
                word[2] == 'h' && word[3] == 'o') {
                echo_mode = true;
            } else {
                write_string("command not found: ");
                write_bytes(word, length);
                line_output = true;
            }
        }
    } else if (echo_mode && length != 0) {
        if (echo_started) {
            write_string(" ");            /* single separator, no leading/trailing */
        }
        echo_started = true;
        write_bytes(word, length);
        line_output = true;
    }

    if (line_end) {
        if (line_output) {
            write_string("\n");           /* blank lines emit no newline */
        }
        line_reset();
    }
}
```

And the read loop becomes:

```c
void minemu_user_main(void) {
    line_reset();
    while (1) {
        write_string("msh> ");
        while (1) {
            uint8_t c;
            int32_t result = ioctl(MINEMU_FD_UART_IN, MINEMU_IOCTL_UART_READ,
                                   (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)&c, 1);
            if (result != 1) {
                continue;
            }
            if (c == '\n') {
                finish_word(true);
                break;
            }
            if (c == 0x08 || c == 0x7f) {
                if (word_index > 0) {
                    --word_index;
                }
                continue;
            }
            if (c == ' ') {
                finish_word(false);
                continue;
            }
            if (word_index < MAX_WORD_LENGTH) {
                word[word_index++] = (char)c;
            } else {
                overflow = true;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Two details doing real work: empty words are skipped rather than resolving the command, so `"   "` emits nothing and `"echo  hi"` doesn't gain a leading space; and `line_output` gates the `\n`, so blank lines emit no newline — which is what makes the `msh> msh> ` adjacency in the editing and overlong assertions hold.
